own_solution.law: Lightly damped harmonic oscillator m x'' + b x' + k x = 0; amplitude envelope A(t) = A0 exp(-b t / (2m)); t = 2m ln(1/0.2) / b
assumptions: envelope ratio independent of release phase and of k

notes: Base: gamma = b/(2m) = 0.2 s^-1, t = ln 5 / 0.2 = 8.047 s. With added 0.19 kg/s damper on the block (present during this run): b = 0.39 kg/s, gamma = 0.39 s^-1, t = 1.6094/0.39 = 4.127 s. k = 60 N/m gives omega0 = 10.95 rad/s >> gamma, consistent with light damping; k enters omega_d but cancels from the envelope (C; could also be read as K with regime underdamped). Sentences T7E76 and TB3BF give the coefficient only as 'small' rather than 0.19 kg/s; if they are intended as variants of TFF7E / T66F6 they differ in the stated value, but since they have no path to the target, this does not change answers. Door sentences are D.
